doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Recording with his own trio, 'Dear Mr. Cole', and getting organized since 2000
summary: He is glad to have his trio on the latest record, mentions Isaiah's success, and says better organization and readable charts changed his working life.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Hey yours looks the same as mine.

I thought it was wonderful that you had your trio on the record. And like people might say well yeah, well of course. But a lot of times people have ringers or whatever, and you have built in ringers.

Yeah I mean I made a record — one of my most successful early records was “Dear Mr. Cole” with Benny Green and Christian McBride. And we never worked together. And we had a great time making the record but I really have to say I’m really pleased that we were able to have the group and bring the group out, especially with Isaiah’s success so early, winning the American Pianist Award and being so popular at the moment and things like that. But he has expressed to me that he likes — wants to stay in the band as long as he can, enjoys playing in the band, I mean and then, you know, it’s a great little group. I mean I love the group. I’ve loved all the groups up until this point, you know I mean so it’s nice to make a — the goal is to try and make records that we can promote like that.

That’s what you said pretty much 23 years ago when we met. I had asked you the question what are your goals in, I said, 15 years. But you said that, that you wanted to keep doing what you’re doing, do it better, be more organized, make some better bread.

So I think the organization part, that part changed my life. I did finally get a stage plot that works. I got the lists of all the different shows that I can do. There’s a big band show, there’s a four horn show, there’s orchestra shows. But the biggest part of the organization was having the charts — a readable chart — which took me forever. I was a bad chart writer and I finally, you know here I still even have this from Jessica’s show the other day. But I didn’t realize, I mean I used to really be — what am I going to do if so-and-so can’t make the date you know. And what am I going to do. And now I’ve made sure — that was the biggest thing is that when you have such a really good group and then Isaiah says, “I’ve got to go promote my record here” I know I can send the set list and the music to somebody and get that — and not worry about it. And then also with a guy like Mike Karn who knows everybody, so you can get this guy, you can get Jeb Patton, you can get Tadataka, you know there are guys out there. That’s the hardest thing, you want to find the guy who can sit down and be in the band you know.
